what: Minecraft's players and server as a state.lifecycle@1 LifecyclePort: the loader's events turned into the contract's crossings (login, logout, respawn, death, dimension change, save, server start and stop), a HostStore for players and one for the server, and durable slots kept in the overworld's saved data. The loader's listeners are the half each loader overlay adds (LoaderEvents); everything else is the same on every loader.

overlays.name: saved-data-type
overlays.why: saved data is a SavedDataType with an Identifier and a codec, the data storage moved to world.level.storage, and a player reaches its server through its level; tags moved to Optional getters at 1.21.5

overlays.name: fabric-1.21
overlays.why: Fabric API: the player and connection events, the entity events (ServerEntityWorldChangeEvents) and the lifecycle events, with phases named by ResourceLocation

overlays.name: fabric-26
overlays.why: Fabric API on 26.x: the same events, the world-change event renamed ServerEntityLevelChangeEvents, phases named by Identifier

overlays.name: neoforge-1.21
overlays.why: NeoForge's PlayerEvent, LivingDeathEvent, LevelEvent and server events on the NeoForge event bus, with an EventPriority

overlays.name: neoforge-26
overlays.why: NeoForge on 26.x: the same events on the NeoForge event bus

overlays.name: forge-1.21
overlays.why: Forge 52: the events on MinecraftForge.EVENT_BUS, with an EventPriority

overlays.name: forge-26
overlays.why: Forge 66: events are records with their own EventBus (BUS.addListener), a priority is a byte, and a cancellable event's listener answers whether to cancel
